newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-PAST AND FUTURE ON DISPLAY AT WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PAST AND FUTURE ON DISPLAY AT WEEKEND.

text.p: The past and future of world rugby union will be on display in three European centres this weekend as the four World Cup semifinalists each swing in to action.
World champions South Africa, minus their inspirational World Cup captain Francois Pienaar and match-winning fly-half Joel Stransky, meet France in Bordeaux on Saturday.
The Springboks edged France in a rain-drenched semifinal in Durban last year.
On the same day England host the New Zealand Barbarians -- an All Black side in all but name -- at Twickenham in a replay of the other semifinal.
Then on Sunday the 1991 champions Australia meet Wales at Cardiff Arms Park in the second of three internationals on their British Isles tour.
Wales have recalled Jonathan Davies at fly-half after an eight-year absence in a selection more pragmatic than sentimental.
At the age of 34, Davies is unlikely to play any part in the 1999 World Cup scheduled for his native country but Welsh coach Kevin Bowring believes he is the man for the job on Saturday.
"Jonathan's recall is a direct result of his outstanding form," Bowring said. "We have long-term goals as well as short term objectives and Jonathan's selection is part of the latter."
Davies, exasperated with the Welsh authorities and anxious for financial security, defected to rugby league in 1989 and enjoyed a distinguished career.

He is clearly now not the quicksilver imp who enchanted the Cardiff Arms' fans in the late 1980s but his time in the gruelling world of professional rugby league has made him a better all-round footballer.
All round footballers are in demand in New Zealand where their visionary coach John Hart is already assembling a squad with the World Cup in mind.
Last year New Zealand initiated nothing short of a rugby revolution in South Africa, unveiling a stunning new generation committed to running the ball at pace from any position.
They stumbled in the final against South Africa, losing in extra time but have continued to practise the running game and this year won their first ever series in South Africa.
Last year Jonah Lomu, Andrew Mehrtens and Josh Kronfeld lit up the South African playing fields.
This year Christian Cullen has burst on to the international scene, scoring his nine tries in 10 appearances for the All Blacks.
Lomu, who is taking antibiotics for a groin infection, and Cullen have been picked for Saturday's match plus another blossoming talent in flanker Andrew Blowers.
Blowers is big enough to pack down at lock, fast enough to play on the wing and is fast acquiring the skills of the absent Zinzan Brooke, possibly the most versatile player in world rugby.

"Saturday is not a test match but it will be a real test of rugby and our attitude to the game," Hart said. "It's an opportunity to show how the game should be played. We invite England to join the party."
England have made a proper mess of entering the professional era, with a long-running dispute between the Rugby Football Union and the leading clubs over who should control the game.
But the crisis appeared to be resolved this week with a typically English compromise, namely inventing another body called NEWCO to administer the sport.
South Africa suffered an early reverse on the French leg of their three-nation tour after comfortably winning all four matches in Argentina.
The Springboks went down 30-22 to the French Barbarians but rallied on Tuesday to defeat a regional XV 36-20.

"They're not going to reinvent rugby, that's for sure," said defeated captain Aubin Hueber. "But what they do, they do well. The pose a formidable physical challenge and never let go. It will be very hard for France."

France are without either of their wings, captain Philippe Saint-Andre and Emile Ntamack plus both locks in Olivier Roumat and Olivier Merle through injury, in effect giving a new generation of Tricolours their chance.

Australia have a talented backline which may yet include their veteran magician David Campese on the wing. Campese, the same age as Davies, was named in a squad of 21 after missing the internationals against Scotland and Ireland.
"If I'm selected, then the Arms' Park is a great place to play rugby," said the world record try scorer.
